title: Token Wisdom · 2026 · Week 23
dek: Verification week: a $1.3T chip selloff, even the CEOs admitting the buildout got ahead of itself — and, quietly, the lab kept working.

epigraph.text: There's no sense in being precise when you don't even know what you're talking about.

editor_note: This week the semiconductor story split in two. On one side, a $1.3 trillion selloff and a chorus — even the CEOs — conceding the AI buildout has gotten ahead of itself. On the other, the breakthroughs that don't trend: a 3D-stacked chip extending Moore's Law, a processor that runs a thousand times faster without the waste heat, Huawei building what the export-control map said was impossible. The market priced the mood. The lab kept working.
recap: The reckoning isn't that AI is overhyped — it's that we keep measuring the wrong thing. Market value moves on sentiment; the substrate moves on physics. When the noise clears, what remains is what always did: who can move electrons, or light, faster and cooler and at scale. This week the answer started to include people the map said it wouldn't.

essay.title: The Sky Has Been Warning Us Since 1859
essay.excerpt: W13 - The sun fired a warning shot in 1859. We had 165 years. We wrote reports, introduced legislation, held hearings — and kept building a bigger antenna. The solution to the oldest infrastructure problem in the modern world exists. It just isn't where anyone thought to look.
essay.pull: We didn't build a civilization since 1859. We built an antenna.
